## Contract review brief — PR #37044 @ `a141c91fb23ee32acda15b2ca0a7e687e189ed20` (card #36349)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #36349: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37044: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `a141c91fb23ee32acda15b2ca0a7e687e189ed20`
  · the check-runs on `a141c91fb23ee32acda15b2ca0a7e687e189ed20`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-objectstack/177ababb-cccd-573a-a846-cda17d8e5bbd/scratchpad/pr-37044/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a141c91fb23ee32acda15b2ca0a7e687e189ed20`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md + none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Inputs: card #36349 (body and all five comments: triage 7076106190, unlock 7107462804, claim 7138250698, dev reports 7138910104 and 7139209343; the card holds no ruling and no earlier contract record), PR #37044 (body, three-file list, net diff), and the check-runs on the head. Read to judge, not reviewed, on `main` at b01d8f97: `ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/lookupAutofill.ts`, `GridField.ts`, `grid-field/GridFieldWidget.tsx`, `LookupField.tsx`, `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/recordFormStamp.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (the `lookupAutofill` describe and its superRefine), `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` (`lookupAutofillTypeMismatch`), and the skill's `evals/objects-fields-relationships.json`. No file in the diff implements or enforces the two `hits` paths, so the scope adds none; the changeset is the lane seat's.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged. The diff holds no schema, validator or gate; what a metadata author can write is the same before and after. Right.
- Public surface: the shipped text of `@objectstack/skills`, two rule files. The change takes back a promise the skill made (an unconditional copy) and states what the runtime has done since #36249; it adds no key, value or type. Right.
- Token ceilings: `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff, so no ceiling moved; the additions are paid inside `field-types.md` and fit `relationships.md`'s existing headroom. Right, and the gate's own verdict is the check-run below.
- Gate verdicts on the head, as concluded when read: every lint.yml lane success (`Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, the three scoped lanes, the aggregate `Lint & Repo Gates`); the four type-check lanes and `TypeScript Type Check` success; `Check Changeset` success (both runs); `PR-body guards` success (both runs); `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; `Check PR Size`, `Build Core`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` success. Not concluded when read: `Test Core (1/10)` and `Test Core (2/10)`, in progress. The diff holds no code and every gate family a skills text diff derives sits in lint.yml, so they do not bear on this judgment; landing still waits on them.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/36349-skills-lookupautofill-currency.md` declares `'@objectstack/skills': patch`. The diff publishes skill text only and changes nothing an author can write (`Metadata-protocol: none`), which takes `patch` under AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3. Right; `Check Changeset` concluded success.
- Clause-②: no is right, with no arm: nothing in the diff widens an accept-set or enlarges a public surface, and nothing narrows one. The PR body and the changeset body carry the same two declaration lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags, from reports 7138910104 and 7139209343:

- Zero token headroom in `field-types.md`, paid by same-file deletion, fourteen table cells outside the `lookupAutofill` paragraph included. Answered: the cells are inside the claimed file, no ceiling moved, and each cell is judged under ④; none loses a hint.
- "left as it was" where the card says "stays empty". Answered, and the dev is right: `judgePickWrites` leaves a refused write out of the patch, `WithheldAutofill.held` carries the value a re-pick left in place and the `lookup.autofillKept` note says the field kept it; the spec describe on `main` says "left as it is". The card's wording would have promised an emptying the runtime does not do.
- A changeset outside the claim's named file surface. Answered: owed by AGENTS.md for a published package; correct level.
- `relationships.md` edited in rework round 1, beyond the claim's file surface. Answered: it is the dev's own round-0 out-of-scope finding (same family, same package), it is a `hits` path and is judged under ④, and the single-writer path guard is green on the head. The widening of the claim is the seat's dispatch act.
- Live eval run NOT MEASURED, against the card's "the skill's evals still pass". Answered: none of the 27 cases in `objects-fields-relationships.json` has a prompt or an assertion on `lookupAutofill`, the grid `autofill` copy or catalog auto-fill. One case reads a trimmed row (case 10 expects `type: 'boolean'`), and that row still says the boolean is the checkbox. No assertion keys on changed text; accepted as not measured.
- PR body stale until the seat applies `pr_body_changes`. Answered: the body read for this record names head a141c91fb2 and carries the `relationships.md` paragraph.
- `git fetch --deepen` on the shared object store, the commit-trailer form, `test:repo` left to CI, the overlap-check timing against PR #36158. Process flags with no trace in the diff; nothing for the contract. The overlap with #36158 on both files is the seat's to re-check at landing.

`open_questions`: empty in both reports. Nothing escalated.

SQL push-down: the diff holds no code, so no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md`, the appended sentences.** "Either copy moves a `currency` amount only between fields in the same currency (`fixed` or per-record); else the target is left as it was and the form says why. Nothing is converted." Held against the code it describes, clause by clause:

- "Either copy": the declared pair (`planDeclaredLookupAutofill`, record form) and the grid's same-named copy plus its declared pairs (`planLookupAutofill`) both end in `judgePickWrites`, which applies `crossCurrencyRefusal` to every candidate write. One rule, both copies.
- "the same currency (`fixed` or per-record)": `amountCurrencyOf` reads the code through `resolveFieldCurrency`, a `fixed` code or the code the record (or the followed parent) holds; `crossCurrencyRefusal` lets a value through only when both sides name the same code, the home currency counting as its configured code.
- "left as it was": a refused write is absent from `plan.patch`; nothing clears the target.
- "the form says why": `LookupField` draws the `lookup-autofill-withheld` note under the field, the grid draws a `line-items-autofill-withheld-N` row under the line, both through `withheldAutofillMessage`, naming the amount and the currencies. `recordFormStamp.ts` stamps the target definitions on every record-form layout (ObjectForm, TabbedForm, WizardForm, ModalForm, DrawerForm, MasterDetailForm, EmbeddableForm), so the rule is live wherever the spec says the key is read.
- "Nothing is converted": no rate is read anywhere on the path; `crossCurrencyRefusal` refuses an implied rate of 1.
- Against the spec it teaches: the `lookupAutofill` describe on `main` states the same CURRENCY RULE for both copies. The skill is a faithful short form of it.
- Against the card's scenario (a home-currency product price picked into a foreign-currency invoice line): source `home`, target a known code, so `differs` (or `noSourceCurrency` when the organization configures no home currency); nothing is written and the note names both. The reader now knows the line takes its price by hand. The card's Done-when is met in two sentences, as it asked.

Tried to break it: two amounts that both declare no currency are "in the same currency" under the sentence and copy in the code (`home` into `home`); a `fixed` code equal to the configured home code copies; a column with `autofill: false` has no same-named copy to judge; the unset, unread and unknown cases all end in the stated outcome (target untouched, reason shown), except an unknown-currency number into a home-currency target, which copies as before and which the sentence does not contradict. None of these breaks the sentence.

**`field-types.md`, the paragraph's two trims.** The example literal became "`unit_price` from a product's `list_price`": the bold lead still spells the pair shape and the direction (target from source) is kept. "(single-value `lookup` / `master_detail`)" became "(single-value only)": see N2.

**`field-types.md`, the fourteen "When to Use" cells.** Each judged for a hint an author needs to pick the type:

- `date` "Date only", `time` "Time only", `datetime` "Date + time": the dropped parentheticals restated "only"; the three rows still tell each other apart.
- `number` "Numeric value", `file` "File attachments": "Generic" marked the fallback; the sibling rows (`currency`, `percent`; `image`, `video`, `audio`) still say what they are for, so the fallback reading stands.
- `markdown` "Markdown content", `html` "Raw HTML", `richtext` "WYSIWYG editor": same meaning.
- `boolean` "Checkbox": the `toggle` row below still reads "distinct UI from checkbox", so the pair is still told apart.
- `location` "Coordinates (lat/lng)": the lat/lng shape, the part an author needs, is kept.
- `avatar` "Profile picture", `signature` "Signature pad", `tags` "Free-form tags": same meaning.
- `slider` "Slider": the closest call, since "Numeric" said what the field stores; the Config cell on the same row (`min`, `max`, `step`) still says it.

No cell loses a hint. No eval case reads these rows beyond case 10, covered under ③.

**`skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`, the Catalog auto-fill bullet.** "(a `currency` amount only in the same currency: field-types.md → `lookupAutofill`)" holds: the same-named copy is the loop in `planLookupAutofill` whose writes go through `judgePickWrites` with the grid's own currency context (`gridAutofillCurrency`). The file's own example (`unit_price: Field.currency()` beside a product lookup) keeps filling, both sides being home-currency amounts; an author who follows the "line in its parent's currency" pattern from `field-types.md` is now told the fill is conditional and where the rule is stated. The pointer follows the cross-file form both files already use, and its target, the bold `lookupAutofill` lead, exists at the head. A pointer rather than a second statement is the right call for one rule with one home.

**The security line.** No changed line teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. Two near misses were checked: the first hunk shows the `password` and `secret` rows as context only, neither is touched; and the paragraph's hunk rewraps the clause "a declared, non-`internal` field of `reference`" word for word (`internal` is a read-protection flag in the spec), so the change teaches nothing about it that `main` does not already say.

Nits, left as accepted deviations (the file has one token of headroom, and neither moves the contract):

- N1 (nit) — the sentence does not say that a `number` side carries no currency and copies as before (`crossCurrencyRefusal` returns early when either side is no amount of money; the spec describe says so in words). A reader may take a `currency` to `number` pair to be withheld when it fills. The card scoped the sentence to currency-to-currency and the sentence is right there.
- N2 (nit) — "(single-value only)" no longer names `lookup` / `master_detail` in the paragraph, while the table above it also holds `tree` and `user`. The Key Config column lists `lookupAutofill` on the `lookup` and `master_detail` rows alone, and the parse refuses the key elsewhere with a message naming both types, so the restriction is still taught one line up and enforced loudly.

Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYo86w1wqy2z2fMrryr`

**VERDICT: PASS**

This is a DELTA record over contract review 7139449788 (PASS at `a141c91fb23ee32acda15b2ca0a7e687e189ed20`). The only change since is one merge of `main` into the branch: commit 63a76475cc, first parent a141c91fb2 (the reviewed head), second parent a68b475bbc (main's tip at the merge), committed by GitHub with a valid signature. Inputs: PR #37044 (body, three-file list, net diff at the new head, both comments), the merge commit and its two parents, main's delta b01d8f97e9..a68b475bbc, and the check-runs on the new head with the log of the lane that runs the token ratchet. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

- The net diff is the reviewed diff, byte for byte. `git diff a68b475bbc 63a76475cc` and `git diff b01d8f97e9 a141c91fb2` name the same three files with the same counts (37 insertions, 23 deletions) and have the same stable patch-id (5ba909d8da3e). At the blob level: `field-types.md` is 252cb4e702 at both heads and 66000636a3 at both bases; `relationships.md` is 43fff87fbf at both heads and cc3304e918 at both bases. The PR's file list on GitHub shows the same three patches. Right.
- The merge carries no hand-written content. The tree of 63a76475cc (8cb1611ea5) equals the tree `git merge-tree` writes for a141c91fb2 and a68b475bbc, and the combined diff is empty: no conflict was resolved, so nothing in the merge is the dev's or the platform's own text.
- Main's delta (5 commits, 82 files) changes `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` in one place only: the `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` ceiling moves 4068 to 4292 with its comment block (#37019, card #36053). The rows for the two scope files are untouched: `field-types.md` 3541 and `relationships.md` 4203 at both heads. Main's delta touches neither scope file, and none of the code the earlier record read to judge them (`lookupAutofill.ts`, `GridField.ts`, `GridFieldWidget.tsx`, `LookupField.tsx`, `recordFormStamp.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`, `stack.zod.ts`, `evals/objects-fields-relationships.json`). Under `skills/` it brings `rules/security.md` and one eval file, both outside this PR's diff.
- Both files stay within their ceilings on the merged tree: `field-types.md` 14160 bytes, 3540 tokens of 3541; `relationships.md` 16805 bytes, 4202 of 4203. The ratchet's own run on the new head prints the same rows (`3540 / 3541 (-1)`, `4202 / 4203 (-1)`, and main's `security.md 4292 / 4292 (+0)`) and ends "60 authored bundle file(s) within their ceilings". One correction to the hand-off: in the tree the ratchet step sits in the `Type Check · source gates` lane of lint.yml, rolled up by `TypeScript Type Check`, not under `Lint & Repo Gates`. That lane's verdict lists the ratchet step `ok`; the lane, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are all success on the new head.
- Check-runs on 63a76475cc: 44, every one completed and every one on this head; 28 success, 16 skipped, none failed, cancelled, neutral or pending. Success: `Lint & Repo Gates` and its eight lint lanes, `TypeScript Type Check` and its four type-check lanes, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `filter`, `Build Core`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Test Core (1/10)`, `Test Core (2/10)`, `Test Core`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. The two Test Core shards the earlier record read as in progress are now concluded, both success, on the new head. The 16 skips are expected: nine UI, docs and database lanes the path filter turns off for a skills-text diff (`Build & E2E UI`, `Plan Test UI shards`, `Type Check UI`, `Lint UI`, the `Test UI` matrix row, `Build UI Deps`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Build Docs`, `Temporal Conformance`), the `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix row and `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the two opt-in harnesses (`18.x upgrade harness`, `Packed-tarball smoke`), the two merge-queue-only verdicts (`Queue verdict`, `Borrowed queue verdict`) and the schedule gate. The same 16 were skipped on the reviewed head.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged. The changeset `.changeset/36349-skills-lookupautofill-currency.md` is in the net diff with the same content (`'@objectstack/skills': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`); `Check Changeset` is success on the new head. The five changesets the merge brings in are main's own and are not in this PR's net diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Every dev flag and both empty `open_questions` lists were answered in 7139449788. The merge adds no dev report and no new flag; the PR body's account of the diff (measured at b01d8f97e9 and a141c91fb2) still matches the net diff.
- SQL push-down: the net diff holds no code, so no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- For the seat, not a finding: `main` has moved three commits past the merged tip (to 938a48f112). None touches the three files of this diff or `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`; this record covers 63a76475cc and nothing later.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` and `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`: identical blobs to the ones judged in 7139449788, and main's delta changes neither the spec text nor the widget code they were held against, so every clause-by-clause finding of that record stands at this head without re-judging.
- The two nits of 7139449788, N1 (the sentence does not say a `number` side carries no currency and copies as before) and N2 ("(single-value only)" no longer names `lookup` / `master_detail` in the paragraph), stay accepted deviations. Neither was touched; `field-types.md` still has one token of headroom and neither moves the contract.
- Security line, judged again: `no`. The PR's net diff is the reviewed one, and no changed hunk in it teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour (the `password` / `secret` rows are context only; the "non-`internal`" clause is rewrapped word for word). The merge brought main's `rules/security.md` rewrite (#37019) onto the branch, but that file is main's landed content, identical on both sides of the net diff, and not a hunk of this PR.
- Rule change: no path under `.claude/**` is in the net diff; `none`.
